title.narrative: From scoping to accreditation: LITA Poultry Curriculum

description.narrative: Poultry is one of the most dynamic and accessible agricultural subsectors in Tanzania, providing income, nutrition and employment for millions of Tanzanians. According to national agricultural sector strategies, over half of household income from animal husbandry in subsistence systems is derived from poultry, underlining its importance for rural livelihoods and food security.One of the core problems is a skills mismatch between what graduates of educational institutes (such as the Livestock Training Agency (LITA)) know and can do, and what the poultry labour market in Tanzania actually needs.After completion of this project, LITA will have a labour-market-oriented, competency-based poultry curriculum that is submitted to the National Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (NACTVET) for accreditation and subsequent roll-out across its campuses. The curriculum will be completed to an accreditation-ready stage: a macro-curriculum plan (programme specification, module outlines, learning outcomes, credit/contact-hour matrix and assessment strategy) prepared in line with NACTVET requirements so it can be submitted for accreditation.Graduates from LITA’s poultry programmes will be better equipped with practical skills and international corporate responsibility (iCSR) awareness that match the needs of commercial and smallholder poultry value-chain actors in Tanzania. In the longer term, this will contribute to higher productivity, safer and more sustainable poultry production and improved income opportunities for youth and women in the sector.
